motion: Is there sufficient evidence to believe in the resurrection of Jesus?

bridges.description: Infer that a bodily resurrection is the most reasonable explanation of the retained historical claims.
Establish death by crucifixion, sincere post-death appearance beliefs, and Paul's conversion experience as historical starting points.
Connect early creedal and narrative attestations to individual and group appearance claims.
Add the claimed majority-supported empty tomb as corroborating evidence beyond the three asserted consensus facts.
Use continued proclamation under persecution to support the sincerity and durability of eyewitness belief.
Argue that the surviving evidence does not overcome the burden needed to infer a resurrection.
Question whether the testimonial sources are firsthand, independent, contemporary, corroborating, and unbiased.
Show that mistake, deception, bereavement experience, or social transmission remain mundane possibilities without committing to one complete reconstruction.
Limit what can be inferred about the Twelve and other alleged witnesses from the attestations discussed.
Challenge the status and evidential force of the empty-tomb arguments, including embarrassment and Mark's literary theme.

sections.title: Historical method and source standards
sections.rationale: Frames how testimony, probability, scholarly agreement, and biblical documents bear on the motion.

sections.title: Minimal facts and limited grants
sections.rationale: Identifies the common ground and the disputed scope of the claimed historical bedrock.

sections.title: Appearance reports and the early creed
sections.rationale: Covers the central evidence that individuals and groups believed they encountered the risen Jesus.

sections.title: Explanatory burden and natural alternatives
sections.rationale: Tests whether resurrection or mundane possibilities better satisfy the motion's sufficiency burden.

sections.title: Sincerity, persecution, and recantation
sections.rationale: Examines whether later suffering supports sincere eyewitness testimony and how broadly that support extends.

sections.title: Empty tomb, embarrassment, and Mark
sections.rationale: Assesses the principal additional line of corroboration and the competing interpretations of its sources.

moves.speaker: Mike Winger
moves.claim: Biblical writings may be used as historical sources without assuming that the Bible is inspired or inerrant.
moves.warrant: Historians extract data from religious texts such as the Quran and Hadith without accepting their theological authority, and the gospel material contains distinct source streams.
moves.inference: The debate may consider biblical texts as historical evidence rather than dismissing them as circular proof.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This span begins with the stated misconception and ends after Winger's explanation of distinct traditions, capturing the complete methodological point.

they're just getting historical data from it
moves.attributionRationale: Continuous opening statement by Mike Winger with no handoff.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed for this clearly attributed continuous opening span.
moves.importanceRationale: The move determines whether the principal documentary evidence is admissible for the motion-level inference.

burdenContact.rationale: It supplies the source basis from which the asserted minimal facts are drawn.

moves.warrant: He cites non-Christian scholars and stresses that crucifixion makes simple revival or swoon explanations less plausible.
moves.inference: A resurrection explanation begins with an actual death rather than mere recovery.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: The span covers the first enumerated fact from its introduction through the explicit statement that death alone is not yet resurrection.

moves.speaker: Mike Winger

moves.warrant: Winger appeals to the First Corinthians 15 creed, its claimed early transmission, and its list of individual and group appearances while distinguishing belief from proof that the appearance was real.
moves.inference: The appearance belief is early rather than a late legendary development and therefore requires explanation.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This complete long argument begins with the second fact, develops the creed and its dating, and ends with Winger's explicit qualification that he is establishing what was preached, not yet its truth.

moves.speaker: Paulogia
moves.claim: Miracles are possible in principle but historically less probable than mundane explanations and therefore require enough evidence to overcome that burden.

moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: The span preserves both Paulogia's explicit possibility concession and his complete comparative-probability burden, avoiding the false claim that he rules miracles impossible.

moves.speaker: Paulogia
moves.claim: A resurrection may explain the evidence, but the discussed facts do not require it and remain adequately explainable by a small number of mistaken or deceptive witnesses.
moves.warrant: Paulogia reiterates that miracles are possible but need much evidence, while Paul's vision and one other claimed experience can seed the reports.
moves.inference: The available evidence is insufficient to believe that a resurrection occurred.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This span covers Paulogia's complete closing from his probability standard through his explicit negative answer to the motion.

moves.attributionRationale: Continuous Paulogia closing statement.
moves.audioVerificationReason: The closing is complete and has no mixed ownership.
moves.importanceRationale: It states the negative's final motion-level conclusion.

burdenContact.rationale: It directly concludes that the sufficiency burden has not been met.

responseComponents.description: Concedes possible explanatory fit while denying evidential necessity or sufficiency.
Maintains that a small number of mundane errors or deceptions still suffices.

moves.speaker: Mike Winger
moves.claim: Unless resurrection is assigned an effectively evidence-proof prior improbability, it remains the most reasonable explanation of the three accepted facts plus the majority-supported empty tomb.
moves.warrant: Winger argues Paulogia has largely accepted the facts and that the main disagreement concerns the prior probability of miracles rather than the resurrection explanation's fit.
moves.inference: The historical evidence is sufficient for resurrection belief absent an antecedent exclusion of miracles.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: The span contains Winger's full closing argument and ends before post-debate courtesies, preserving his best-explanation and worldview claims.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it is actually the best explanation
then i have a really good historical case for the resurrection of jesus
moves.attributionRationale: Continuous Mike Winger closing statement.
moves.audioVerificationReason: The closing is complete; Paulogia's actual possibility concession is separately preserved to avoid adopting Winger's characterization.
moves.importanceRationale: It states the affirmative's final motion-level inference.

burdenContact.rationale: It directly concludes that the evidence is sufficient if miracles remain live possibilities.

responseComponents.description: Argues that the negative's probability standard, rather than explanatory fit, drives the contrary conclusion.
